dimension: D03-failures — Unhandled failure modes / error paths
summary: The ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT has NO dedicated failure-mode section. The EVENT_MODEL §23 contract (8 rows) and RISKS.md (13 technical risks) define the failure surface, but the draft only resolves a subset, and scatters those resolutions across §6 (module table), §10 (background jobs), §12, §13, and §14 (testing). Several load-bearing runtime failure paths are asserted-but-unspecified: they appear as a desired property, a state-machine enum value, or a test bullet, with no owner + behavior pinned in the binding architecture body. The two most serious: (1) event-write-fail / fail-closed is stated only as a TEST assertion (§14) with no architectural specification of which actions are 'audit-required', what 'fail closed' returns to the caller, or what the agent/UI sees; (2) agent crash, PTY death mid-session, and Codex app-server disconnect (all DISTINCT from the ADR-010 daemon-restart case, since the daemon is ALIVE) have no recovery contract at all — ADR-010 only covers daemon restart/crash. integration auth-expiry/rate-limit, stale-precondition-between-preview-and-execute, lease-expiry-of-paused-holder user experience, projection-corruption rebuild trigger, and network loss are also under-specified as owned behaviors.

findings.finding: Event-write-fail / fail-closed is the #1 durability invariant in EVENT_MODEL §23 ('Action should fail closed if audit is required') but the draft NEVER specifies it as an architectural behavior — it appears ONLY as a Gateway test-suite bullet in §14 ('fail-closed-on-audit-write'). There is no owner, no definition of which actions/events are 'audit-required' vs best-effort, no spec of what the caller (agent via can_use_tool, UI, Brain) receives when the write fails, and no statement of whether the in-flight executor's side effect (e.g. a git mutation already applied) is rolled back when the post-execution event write fails. THREAT_MODEL T-08 leans on append-only single-writer audit as a security control, so a silently-dropped event is a security gap, not just a correctness one.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 line 234: 'Gateway tests: ... fail-closed-on-audit-write.' is the ONLY occurrence of fail-closed in the draft (grep confirmed). EVENT_MODEL §23 row 1 mandates the behavior. The draft §6 eventstore module ('append events + projections + outbox in one txn') describes the happy path but never the txn-failure path. DATA_MODEL §2.5 says event+projection+outbox commit in one txn but is silent on commit failure semantics.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §Event Store & Concurrency Model (or a new §Failure-Mode Contract) a binding fail-closed rule: (a) define 'audit-required actions' = all Gateway actions at risk >= 1 (all mutations); (b) specify that the executor MUST commit the authoritative ActionExecution* event in the SAME transaction boundary as, or strictly before acknowledging, the mutation — and that an event-write failure aborts the action with a typed GatewayError returned to the caller; (c) state the rollback/compensation rule when a side effect already applied but its terminal event cannot be written (e.g. emit ActionPartiallySucceeded best-effort, surface a hard 'audit integrity' alert); (d) cross-reference EVENT_MODEL §23 row 1.

findings.finding: Agent crash, PTY death mid-session, and Codex app-server disconnect — all with the DAEMON ALIVE — have NO recovery contract. ADR-010 / §12 / §7 only cover the daemon-restart/crash case (resume-or-replay). The EVENT_MODEL taxonomy has SessionFailed (§10.9), TerminalProcessExited and TerminalPTYFailed (§10.10) events, and RISKS.md TR-01 is scoped to 'survival across daemon restart' — but the inverse-and-more-common case (the supervised child or its pipe dies while the daemon keeps running) is unowned. There is no spec for: does the daemon auto-resume a crashed Claude/Codex process, surface SessionFailed and wait, or relaunch? What happens to an in-flight ActionRequest whose executing agent just died? For Codex specifically the app-server stdio pipe can drop independently of a crash (RISKS TR-02 churn) and re-association is via thread/list?cwd= — but that re-association is only specified for restart recovery (DATA_MODEL §5), not for a live mid-session disconnect.
findings.evidence: ADR-010 (DECISIONS.md lines 226-229) is explicitly two-tier: 'UI restart (daemon alive)' and 'Daemon restart / crash' — neither is 'agent process dies, daemon alive'. EVENT_MODEL §10.10 lists TerminalPTYFailed with no behavior; §737-743 only says don't store raw terminal output as events. grep for 'agent crash'/'PTY death'/'app-server disconnect' in the draft returns nothing. RISKS.md TR-01 title is 'PTY / session survival across daemon restart'. DATA_MODEL §4.1 Session state machine has 'failed' but the transition trigger SessionFailed has no recovery owner.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §Session Lifecycle & Survival a third recovery tier: 'supervised child failure (daemon alive)'. Specify per harness: (a) the daemon's session/terminal supervisor detects child exit (process-group reaper, §10) and emits SessionFailed + TerminalProcessExited/TerminalPTYFailed; (b) whether NexusOps auto-attempts harness resume (claude --resume / codex thread/resume) vs surfacing a 'restart session' affordance in the Human Input Queue; (c) the fate of any in-flight ActionRequest owned by the dead session (mark ActionFailed, release its lease/fencing token); (d) for Codex, distinguish app-server pipe-drop (reconnect + thread/list?cwd= re-associate) from a true Codex process crash (relaunch). Reconcile with RISKS TR-01/TR-02.

findings.finding: Integration auth-expiry and rate-limit have a STATE but no BEHAVIOR. ExecutionProfile and integration state machines carry 'auth_expired' and 'rate_limited' (DATA_MODEL §4.8), and §9 mentions 'Linear 24h refresh' and a 'budget query complexity (10k-point cap)', but the draft never specifies the runtime failure path: what happens to an in-flight outbox-driven GitHub/Linear action (or a session.create) when the token is expired or the provider returns 401/403/429? Does the outbox retry with backoff (DATA_MODEL §2.5 says backoff but not error classification), surface an approval-style 're-auth required' to the user, or fail the ActionRequest? GitHub secondary-rate-limit (Retry-After) and Linear 429 are normal operating conditions, not edge cases. THREAT_MODEL T-13 mandates 'hard fail, no plaintext fallback' on keychain failure but the draft body doesn't carry that as an owned behavior either.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §9 line 188 mentions '24h refresh' and '10k-point cap' but no failure path. DATA_MODEL §4.8 ExecutionProfile states 'rate_limited | auth_expired' with note 'set by adapter telemetry + keychain self-test' but no consumer behavior. §10 'Outbox drainers ... backoff/retry' does not classify retryable (429/5xx) vs terminal (401/403) errors. EVENT_MODEL §10.6 has GitHubSyncFailed/LinearSyncFailed events but the draft assigns them no handling. EVENT_MODEL §23 has no row for integration auth/rate-limit at all (a gap the draft inherits).
findings.proposed_fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md §Integration Architecture an explicit integration-failure contract: (a) classify provider errors into transient (429 honoring Retry-After, 5xx → outbox backoff) vs terminal (401/403 → emit *SyncFailed + transition ExecutionProfile/integration to auth_expired/rate_limited + surface a 're-authenticate' card in the Human Input Queue, do NOT silently drop the outbox row → mark 'dead' only after a bounded retry budget); (b) the fate of the originating ActionRequest (ActionFailed with a retryable flag); (c) keychain-unavailable → hard fail per T-13. Add a corresponding row to EVENT_MODEL §23.

findings.finding: Stale-precondition between preview and execute (ACTION_GATEWAY §16.4) is asserted but its owned behavior is only a TEST bullet. The draft §14 lists 'stale-precondition re-check' as a Gateway test, and §8 (flows) shows preview→approve→execute, but the architecture body never specifies: (a) WHEN preconditions are re-checked (at approval grant? at executor entry after lock acquisition, per AG §16.3 'a queued action must re-check preconditions after acquiring lock'?), (b) WHAT happens on a mismatch — AG §16.4 says 'stop and refresh preview', but the draft doesn't say whether that re-enters AwaitingApproval (forcing re-approval) or auto-re-previews, and (c) whether the human's prior approval is invalidated when the diff changed underneath them (a security-relevant case: approving diff A but executing diff B). The git source-of-truth rule (DATA_MODEL §3 'never trust the cache for a mutation decision — re-read git2 before acting') implies the mechanism but doesn't bind the Gateway lifecycle to it.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §14 line 234 'stale-precondition re-check' (test only). ACTION_GATEWAY §16.4 defines the requirement and §16.3 says re-check after lock. The Gateway lifecycle in AG §8 has no explicit re-validation state between Approved and Executing. The draft §6 gateway row ('normalize → resolve resources → policy → preview → approval → execute') has no re-check step between approval and execute.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md §Action Gateway an explicit lifecycle step: after lock+fencing-token acquisition and immediately before executor.execute(), re-resolve resources and re-evaluate preconditions (git2 live re-read per DATA_MODEL §3); on mismatch, abort with ActionFailed(reason=stale_precondition), regenerate the preview, and REQUIRE fresh approval if the previewed diff/resource changed (never execute a different mutation than the one approved). Bind this to ACTION_GATEWAY §16.4/§16.3 and the SessionWaitingOnPermission flow.

findings.finding: Lease expiry of a paused/stalled holder is well-covered at the mechanism level (fencing tokens, RISKS TR-06, DATA_MODEL §2.6) but the USER-FACING failure path is unspecified. The draft guarantees an executor 'rejects any mutation carrying a stale (lower) token', but never says what the rejected, formerly-paused session/agent experiences, or what the human sees. RISKS TR-06 fallback says 'on any fencing-token rejection, surface a hard conflict to the user rather than auto-resolving' — but that mitigation is in RISKS.md, not landed as owned behavior in the draft body. Without it, a resumed stale session silently fails its mutation with no UX, contradicting EVENT_MODEL §14 audit-display requirements and the 'no invisible mutation' principle's inverse (no invisible mutation FAILURE).
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §6 locks row ('monotonic fencing tokens (mandatory)') and §14 ('fencing-token rejection of stale holders' test) but the user-facing conflict path appears only in RISKS.md TR-06 fallback (line 95), not the draft body. RISKS.md TR-06 also notes 'Lease holdership is projectable to the UI' as a should, not a spec'd projection. The 8 MVP projections (DATA_MODEL §2.3) do not include a lease/conflict projection.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md §Locking & Leases the binding rejection contract: a stale-fencing-token mutation emits ActionFailed(reason=fencing_conflict) + a conflict event, transitions the rejected session to a 'blocked/conflict' state, and surfaces a hard-conflict card in the Human Input Queue (NOT auto-resolved). State whether lease holdership ('who holds this worktree') is exposed via a projection or the WorktreeProjection's owner_session_id. Promote RISKS TR-06 fallback into binding behavior.

findings.finding: Brain sidecar crash mid-proposal / mid-tool-call is under-specified relative to the steady-state degradation case. The draft (§13, RISKS TR-11) covers Brain ABSENT/STALE well ('degrades gracefully', 'drawer shows Brain unavailable'), and §10 has a 'Sidecar supervisor' (ping + restart/backoff). But the IN-FLIGHT failure is unowned: if the Brain crashes DURING a brain.ask / brain.sync / action-plan proposal (i.e. a daemon→Brain MCP call is outstanding), what does the caller get? Is the in-flight brain.* ActionRequest failed, retried after respawn, or left hanging? MCP stdio call timeouts are not specified. Also unspecified: a half-emitted BrainActionPlanProposed whose Brain process dies before the plan is fully streamed.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §13 line 226 + RISKS TR-11 cover absent/stale (steady state). §10 line 207 'Sidecar supervisor — Brain MCP ping + restart/backoff + process-group kill' covers liveness but not in-flight-request fate. EVENT_MODEL §10.13 has BrainIndexFailed but no Brain-RPC-timeout/crash-mid-call event. OQ-BR-10 ('How does Brain handle unavailable/stale platform data') is tagged P1 and addresses the inverse direction (Brain reading platform), not platform's outstanding call to a crashing Brain.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md §Project Brain Seam an in-flight-failure clause: every daemon→Brain MCP call carries a timeout; on timeout or pipe EOF, the corresponding brain.* ActionRequest is failed (ActionFailed, retryable=true for idempotent queries), the supervisor respawns per backoff, and partially-streamed proposals are discarded (never persisted as a usable ActionPlan). Specify that a Brain crash never blocks the core loop (already locked) AND never leaves a dangling 'executing' Brain action.

findings.finding: Projection corruption / rebuild trigger lacks a detection owner. EVENT_MODEL §23 row 2 ('Projection update fails → projection marks degraded and can rebuild') and §13.2 ('Projection corruption should not corrupt raw events') are referenced, and DATA_MODEL §7.2 specifies the rebuild MECHANISM (truncate + replay, degraded state, skip bad event). But the draft never specifies HOW corruption/divergence is DETECTED (a projector exception is caught, but silent logical divergence — a projection that is wrong-but-not-erroring — has no detection), nor WHO triggers a rebuild (manual UI action? startup-only? a checksum?). The 'projection rebuild UI' is explicitly P1 (EVENT_MODEL §25), so in MVP a corrupted projection has no user-invokable recovery — only a code-driven projector_version bump (DATA_MODEL §6.4/§7.1). This leaves a real MVP gap: a projection that silently diverges from the event log cannot be repaired by the user.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §7.2 covers rebuild mechanism + degraded handling on projector ERROR/unknown-version, but not silent divergence detection. EVENT_MODEL §25 lists 'projection rebuild UI' as P1 (deferred). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §18.2 does not list projection-rebuild among deferred items explicitly, creating ambiguity about whether MVP has ANY rebuild trigger. §6 projections row says 'degraded handling' but not detection of non-erroring corruption.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md §Event Store & Concurrency Model (projections) the MVP rebuild trigger: (a) on startup, validate projection_offsets.schema_version vs projector code version → auto-rebuild on mismatch; (b) provide at least a debug/CLI rebuild command for MVP even though the rebuild UI is P1; (c) state the MVP detection scope honestly — error/unknown-version → degraded marker + skip; silent logical divergence is NOT auto-detected in MVP (document as a known limitation) — so finalize doesn't over-claim crash-recoverability. Reconcile §18.2 deferred list.

findings.finding: Daemon crash MID-ACTION (executor partway through a non-atomic side effect) is not addressed as a recovery path. ADR-010 covers session survival and 'locks reclaimed via expired leases', and idempotency keys (AG §16.1) prevent double-apply on RETRY — but the draft never specifies recovery for an ActionRequest left in 'executing' status when the daemon died after the external side effect (e.g. git push succeeded, or octocrab PR created) but before the terminal ActionSucceeded event committed. On restart, does the daemon detect orphaned 'executing' action_requests rows and reconcile (re-check the real git/GitHub state to decide succeeded-vs-failed), retry via idempotency key, or mark them failed? Without this, the audit log can permanently disagree with reality (a PR exists but the event says 'executing'), undermining EVENT_MODEL §3.2 auditability and the source-of-truth matrix.
findings.evidence: DATA_MODEL §2.9 action_requests.status includes 'executing' but §7.2 'Recovery on daemon restart' (line 631) lists projection rebuild, git2 re-read, Brain ping, harness resume, lease reclaim — NOT orphaned-in-flight-action reconciliation. AG §16.1 idempotency prevents double-apply on retry but nothing triggers the retry/reconcile after a mid-action crash. The transactional-outbox (DATA_MODEL §2.5) guarantees event+outbox atomicity for RECORDING, but an external side effect (push/PR) is NOT inside the SQLite txn, so a crash between side-effect and event-commit is possible.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to ARCHITECTURE.md §Backend / Daemon recovery (and §Action Gateway) an orphaned-action reconciliation step on daemon restart: scan action_requests WHERE status='executing'; for each, re-derive real-world state via the executor's idempotency key (git2 re-read / octocrab GET / lease check) and transition to succeeded/failed accordingly, emitting the missing terminal event. State which executors are reconcilable vs which must be surfaced to the user as 'unknown outcome'. Cross-reference EVENT_MODEL §23 (add a 'daemon crash mid-action' row).

findings.finding: Network loss (offline operation) is asserted as a principle (EVENT_MODEL §4.3 / §2 'must work offline') but the draft never specifies the degraded UX for the integration-dependent features. When the machine is offline, GitHub/Linear reads (projection refresh), PR creation, and OAuth refresh all fail; the local cockpit (sessions/terminals/git/Gateway) should keep working. The draft implies this (outbox-driven writes queue, reads cached as projections) but never states it as an owned behavior, nor what the user sees for stale integration projections vs the local-truth surfaces. This is lower severity because the outbox + projection-cache architecture makes the behavior mostly emergent, but it is not pinned.
findings.evidence: EVENT_MODEL §4.3 'The desktop app must work offline' (principle). ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §9 'reads cached as projections' + 'integration writes are Gateway actions drained via the outbox' imply queueing but no explicit offline contract. EVENT_MODEL §23 row 'Remote sync fails → keep local truth; remote projections become stale visibly' covers the sync-mirror case but not interactive integration calls (PR create while offline). No 'offline' or 'network loss' string in the draft body (grep confirmed).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a short clause to ARCHITECTURE.md §Integration Architecture: offline = local cockpit (sessions/terminals/git/Gateway/Brain) fully operational; integration reads serve last-known projection with a 'stale (offline)' badge; integration WRITES (create PR/issue) queue in the outbox and drain on reconnect (subject to idempotency), with the originating ActionRequest shown as 'queued (offline)' rather than failed. Bind to EVENT_MODEL §23 'Remote sync fails' row.

findings.finding: The draft inherits EVENT_MODEL §23's failure table but never reproduces or binds it, so the duplicate-event, unknown-event-type, corrupt-payload, and clock-skew rows have no owner in the architecture. These are mostly handled implicitly (DATA_MODEL §2.1 ux_events_idempotency unique index for dedup; §7.2 unknown-version skip; §2.1 seq + occurred_at/recorded_at for clock skew), but a finalizer reading ARCHITECTURE.md alone would not find a single place asserting these as binding behaviors with the responsible module named. EVENT_MODEL §23's 'Corrupt payload → quarantine event' has the thinnest coverage — artifacts has a 'quarantined' redaction_status (DATA_MODEL §2.7) but there is no event-row quarantine path.
findings.evidence: EVENT_MODEL §23 rows: Duplicate event (idempotency), Unknown event type (store raw, flag, don't crash), Corrupt payload (quarantine + audit integrity warning), Clock skew (occurred_at + recorded_at). DATA_MODEL covers dedup (§2.1) and version-skip (§7.2) but 'corrupt payload quarantine' for an EVENT (not an artifact) is absent. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT has no consolidated failure-mode table.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a single ARCHITECTURE.md §Failure-Mode Contract table that reproduces EVENT_MODEL §23's 8 rows PLUS the gaps found in this audit (event-write-fail caller behavior, agent/PTY/app-server child failure, integration auth/rate-limit, daemon-crash-mid-action, fencing-conflict UX), each with an OWNING MODULE (§6) and the binding behavior — so the contract lives in one auditable place. Add an event-row quarantine path (corrupt payload_json → quarantine table/flag + audit-integrity event), distinct from the artifacts quarantine.
